diagnosis: Stable angina due to coronary artery disease

patient.name: David Shaw
patient.life_story: David works part-time as a library assistant after many years at a busy post office. He enjoys gardening and keeps notes about appointments and symptoms. Since the discomfort began, he has searched online and talked it through repeatedly with his family.

personality.description: David is worried, speaks at length, adds side details, and often seeks reassurance. He responds well when the student acknowledges his worry and gently structures the conversation.

symptoms: Intermittent central chest pressure or tightness began about three months ago; it happens two or three times most weeks and the pattern has not noticeably changed.
The pressure sometimes spreads toward the left shoulder and upper arm. Each episode lasts about three to five minutes and feels moderate, around five out of ten.
Episodes come on with brisk walking, hills, carrying heavy items, or cold weather. They settle within about five minutes after he stops and rests.
He sometimes feels mildly short of breath during an episode. He has no chest discomfort now and has not had episodes while resting or asleep; the last episode was two days ago.
medical_history: High blood pressure diagnosed about seven years ago.
High cholesterol diagnosed about two years ago; no previous diagnosed heart attack, angina, or coronary procedure.
medications: Glyceryl trinitrate (GTN) spray prescribed by his GP for the episodes about six weeks ago.
family_history: His father had a heart attack; David does not volunteer the exact age at first.
lifestyle: Lives with his husband, Paul; his adult daughter visits most weekends.
Usually has one or two beers at the weekend.
Smokes cigarettes; initially gives a vague answer about how much. The amount and duration are held in secrets.
secrets: Smokes about 20 cigarettes a day and has done so for roughly 30 years.
His father's heart attack happened when his father was 54.
Often misses two or three atorvastatin doses in a week.
Fears the symptoms could be a serious heart problem and worries about being unable to work or garden.
Has stopped gardening alone because he worries he could have an episode without anyone nearby.
